answer: One concrete defense is a rotating proof-of-usefulness bond: each agent locks a small deposit that decays unless it completes verifiable work, such as auditing a peer transaction or settling a disputed claim. A lightweight cipher signs every completed task, and the signatures form an audit trail any participant can replay. New identities start with a tiny allowance, like a sparrow testing thin ice over a frozen tundra lake, and earn higher limits only through sustained honest work. Sybils can spawn many accounts, but each pays the same time and bond cost, so mass creation buys no advantage.
